findings.title: Empty columns/data passed to TableWidgetVisualization behind feature flag
findings.body: When the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature flag is enabled, `TableWidgetVisualization` is rendered with `columns={[]}` and `tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}}`. The real data (`result.data`, `result.meta`, `fields`, etc.) that the prior branch passed to `StyledSimpleTableChart` is dropped on this branch. Any organization with the flag enabled will see a completely empty dashboard table instead of their actual rows. This branch should pass the same columns/tableData derived from `result.meta` and `result.data` that the existing branch uses.

findings.title: Visualize API silently breaks multi-y-axis support and changes stacking behavior
findings.body: The `Visualize` constructor now takes a single `yAxis: string` instead of `yAxes: readonly string[]`, and `this.stack = 'all'` is now unconditional. Previously, bar charts with multiple y-axes rendered with `stack === undefined` (unstacked), and `Visualize.replace({yAxes: [...]})` could mutate the y-axis list. Any saved view, link, or component that constructs `new Visualize([...])` or `replace({yAxes: [...]})` will silently produce wrong data or fail. Additionally, callers of `Visualize.fromJSON(json)` previously received a single `Visualize`; the new signature returns `Visualize[]`. Code that did `Visualize.fromJSON(x).replace(...)` will break (`.replace` is undefined on an array). This is a breaking change to a user-facing feature and should be called out in the PR description / release notes.

findings.title: Renaming analytics event 'replay.view_html' to 'replay.view-html' breaks downstream consumers
findings.body: `trackAnalytics('replay.view_html', ...)` is renamed to `trackAnalytics('replay.view-html', ...)`. The internal type registry in `replayAnalyticsEvents.tsx` is updated to match, but any external dashboards, alerts, or saved queries that filter on the old `replay.view_html` event name will silently stop receiving data. Renaming a published analytics event key is an API contract break and should be deprecated, not renamed silently, or at minimum called out clearly in the release notes.

findings.title: Analytics recorded before feature flag check, inflating metrics
findings.body: `analytics.record('preprod_artifact.api.assemble', ...)` is invoked unconditionally at the top of `post()` before the `features.has('organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble', ...)` check. Requests from organizations that don't have the feature enabled will still emit analytics events, polluting the metric with traffic that never reached the assemble path. The record call should happen after the feature flag passes (or guarded by the same condition).

findings.title: Broad `except Exception` in get_environment_info silently swallows errors
findings.body: `get_environment_info` wraps its entire body (including `issue.get_recommended_event()` and `recommended_event.get_environment()`) in `except Exception`, only logs at info level, and returns an empty string. If anything in the recommended-event / environment lookup regresses, this will silently drop environment info from every GitHub/GitLab suspect-PR comment with no alert. At minimum, narrow the catch to the specific exceptions that can be raised (e.g. `Group.DoesNotExist`, `Environment.DoesNotExist`) and/or log at warning/error level.

findings.title: ParameterizationRegexExperiment removed without deprecation
findings.body: The `ParameterizationRegexExperiment` class is removed from `__all__`, the `ParameterizationExperiment` union type alias no longer includes it, and the option `grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent` is deleted. Any external consumer or downstream test that still references `ParameterizationRegexExperiment` will fail with `ImportError` or `TypeError`. If this class is genuinely unused, this is fine, but the public export should be removed deliberately and a deprecation cycle would be safer given `__all__` is exported.

findings.title: fetch_error_details pairs zipped IDs with nodestore values that may be out of order or duplicated
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` does `for event_id, data in zip(error_ids, events.values())`, relying on `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids).values()` to return entries in the same order as `node_ids`. If `nodestore.backend.get_multi` returns a mapping whose iteration order does not strictly match the request order (some cache backends do not guarantee this), or if `error_ids` contains duplicates and the implementation deduplicates internally, then `event_id` and `data` will be mismatched: the wrong title/timestamp/message will be associated with the wrong event id when feeding error context to the LLM. Iterate `events` by explicit node_id lookup (e.g. `[events.get(nid) for nid in node_ids]`) to make ordering explicit.

findings.title: Removal of 'browser_report_received' info log not covered by remaining tests
findings.body: The previous endpoint logged `logger.info('browser_report_received', extra={'request_body': request.data})` for every accepted request. The new endpoint removes this log. The test file drops `test_logs_request_data_if_option_enabled` and the new `test_basic` does not assert any logger.info behavior. If the original intent of the endpoint was to capture raw browser reports (the PR description for the original feature indicated GCP forwarding), this log loss should be intentional and documented, or the test asserting the log should be retained.

findings.title: noise_config added to DBQueryInjectionVulnerabilityGroupType without comment
findings.body: A `noise_config = NoiseConfig(ignore_limit=5)` is added to `DBQueryInjectionVulnerabilityGroupType` without any inline comment explaining why this group type is being treated as noisy at a 5-event limit. Group-type noise configs are product decisions that affect alerting/grouping behavior and should be reviewed; at minimum a comment should explain the rationale so future maintainers don't remove it by mistake.

findings.title: MatchedRow.max_segment_id type change lacks test for the None branch
findings.body: `MatchedRow` is updated so `max_segment_id: int | None`, and `_make_recording_filenames` short-circuits when it is `None`. The corresponding test change only flips an existing fixture from `0` to `None` to exercise the early return, but does not assert that no deletion request is made when `max_segment_id` is `None` (no chunks produced, archive-only path). A regression that deletes despite `None` would not be caught by the existing test as-is.
